question: Chain a FLOAT-ARITHMETIC body end to end, all five links, and establish whether IEEE 754 binary64 arithmetic is expressible in EvalIR.
why_this_one_of_the_four: It is the ONLY float operator whose semantics contradicts its integer sibling in the same ir_binop_eval: udiv on a zero divisor is IROutcome.ub IRFault.div_zero; fdiv on a zero divisor is a signed infinity. Registering it proves the float lane is not a rename of the integer lane, and both are executed side by side as kernel witnesses.
It is non-commutative, so operand ORDER is semantically observable - 0.0/1.0 is +0.0 where 1.0/0.0 is +inf, both executed.
Its exactly-determined fragment is the largest of the four: every one of the 4x4 class combinations has a determined answer except 0/0 and inf/inf (invalid operations) and fin/fin (rounding).
It is the LAST flip of the crate (flipped_so_far=209).

IS_FLOAT_ARITHMETIC_EXPRESSIBLE_IN_EVALI.answer: PARTLY. A real evaluation case exists and is registered; a total one is refused, and each refusal has a distinct reason.
IS_FLOAT_ARITHMETIC_EXPRESSIBLE_IN_EVALI.build_item_delivered: crates/clean-verify/src/spec/core_spec/eval_ir_float.rs - the binary64 VALUE DOMAIN: IRF64Class (nan_/inf_/zero_/fin_), ir_f64_class over a sign/magnitude split, the four classified operation tables ir_f64_{add,sub,mul,div}_at, and the typed dispatcher ir_float_binop. ir_binop_eval's fadd/fsub/fmul/fdiv arms now compute instead of returning the blanket ir_float_fault. IRFault gained `not_float` (APPENDED, no constructor position moves) so an ill-formed operand (type_error) stays distinguishable from a well-formed input this semantics declines (unmodelled).
modelled: x / 0 = +-inf at the XOR sign (IEEE 754-2019 7.3 divideByZero: an EXACT infinity)
0 / x, x / inf = +-0 at the XOR sign; inf / x = +-inf
inf * x and x * inf (x nonzero) = +-inf; 0 * x and x * 0 (x not inf) = +-0
inf + x, x + inf (finite or same-signed inf) = that infinity
x +- 0 and 0 +- x for finite x (adding a zero is exact, subnormals included)
(-0)+(-0) = -0 and every other zero pair = +0 (6.3 roundTiesToEven)
x + (-x) for finite x = +0 (6.3: an exact zero sum is +0) - the only finite+finite case the standard fixes without rounding

refused_with_reasons.any NaN result: The payload of a quiet NaN is IMPLEMENTATION-DEFINED (6.2.3 says `should`). A wall in the STANDARD, not in the model: no bit pattern is determined, so there is nothing to return.
refused_with_reasons.inf - inf, 0 * inf, 0/0, inf/inf: invalid operations -> a NaN -> the same wall
refused_with_reasons.finite (+,-,*,/) finite, except the exac: needs round-to-nearest-even over a 53-bit significand. NOT AFFORDABLE: aligning and renormalising walks values of magnitude 2^53 and every ir_nat_* is a unary Nat.rec walk. Buying it with the kernel-native Nat.div/Nat.mod/Nat.beq would add ACCELERATED CONSTANTS whose declared bodies the kernel never consults - speed bought with trust - which eval_ir_state already refuses for ir_nat_rem.
refused_with_reasons.any binary format but binary64: binary32/binary16 have different exponent fields and different boundary constants. IRTy.float_ w carries w and ir_float_binop decides only w = 64; every other width is the tagged unmodelled verdict.

IS_FLOAT_ARITHMETIC_EXPRESSIBLE_IN_EVALI.what_made_it_affordable: Every classification test is ir_nat_ltb / ir_nat_eqb / ir_nat_pos, and those comparisons are FOLDED: one native BigNat Nat.sub plus one iota step, with ir_nat_ltb_walk_eq and ir_nat_eqb_walk_eq proving each is the same predicate as the paired unary walk it replaced. Through the walk, deciding the sign of an infinity would peel 9.2e18 Nat.rec layers.
IS_FLOAT_ARITHMETIC_EXPRESSIBLE_IN_EVALI.new_trust_added: none - Nat.add and Nat.sub were already relied on by ir_nat_pow2 and ir_nat_rem
IS_FLOAT_ARITHMETIC_EXPRESSIBLE_IN_EVALI.note_on_costs: 25 of 25 candidates elaborated and kernel-checked against one EvalIR-bundle spec build (13.7 s). Not one exceeds 0.05 s, which is the whole point: the same declarations through ir_nat_ltb would be unreachable by a factor of about a billion.

what_is_NOT_claimed: ir_f64_div is NOT proved to be f64::div. It is IEEE 754 on the classified fragment by construction and by reading, and a tagged refusal elsewhere. The gap is the same SHAPE as the one env_is_valid_char states (a u64-level specification, not the Unicode predicate) and it is LARGER, because a float format has more structure than an interval test.

theorem_shape.A4: ir_fd_correct - TOTAL over a PARTIAL domain. For every pair of bit patterns, every environment pointer, every heap, every next-address counter and every fuel >= 2, ir_eval returns exactly ir_fd_res (env_reduce_float_div a b): the value where the fragment is modelled and IROutcome.unmodelled IRFault.float_domain where it is not. The FIRST chain whose A4 conclusion is not an IROutcome.ret.
theorem_shape.A5: ir_fd_machine_sound (inversion off the returned float), ir_fd_machine_sound_divzero (reaching THE ARGUMENTS: a finite dividend over a zero divisor answers the infinity at the XOR sign - the fact that makes float division a different operation from integer division, stated about the artifact).
theorem_shape.corollaries: ir_fd_returns_iff_modelled (the refusal boundary as an equality of Bools, so neither direction can be weakened) and ir_fd_never_traps (no UB, no type error, no stuck state, no exhaustion, on ANY pair of bit patterns including invalid f64 encodings).
theorem_shape.new_machinery: ir_run_le_ret is stated for IROutcome.ret and cannot be widened in place - the unconditional monotonicity form is FALSE because a run that exhausts at f may halt at succ f. ir_fd_run_succ / ir_fd_run_le are the same induction at the ir_fd_res image, with ir_fd_fuelout_absurd (by IROption.rec, through a new fuel_out != unmodelled discriminator and the existing fuel_out != ret one) showing that image never contains fuel_out.

the_clobber_and_its_lesson.what_happened: The eighth-chain commit was built with git commit-tree over a tree read from origin/main AFTER that ref advanced to d11d2cb77, but with file contents from a worktree based on 71e1ce8be. Three of the 19 staged paths carried newer content and were silently reverted.
the_clobber_and_its_lesson.why_the_check_did_not_catch_it: The push script verified that exactly the 19 intended paths DIFFER from the base. That is a path-set check, not a diff-path-by-path check: it is silent about content you overwrote, precisely because those paths are the ones you meant to change.
the_clobber_and_its_lesson.the_check_that_would_have: for every path staged, either it is new, or its blob in the push base equals its blob at the commit the worktree was built from
